text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The caretaker cabinet has decided to undertake a comprehensive reform programme for the banking and financial sectors to deal with the bad assets of state-run banks and financial institutions through a Resolution Trust Corporation.
- OUsted prime minister Benazir Bhutto has asked President Farooq Leghari to prove his innocence in a special court as required under the recently promulgated Ehtasab (accountability) Ordinance.

- The Lahore High Court has sought the record of the stables built in the Prime Minister's House in Islamabad to ascertain whether public funds were involved in their construction or in feeding and breeding of the horses kept there.

- The ceretaker cabinet said the demand by ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto to have a say in any agreement signed with the International Monetary Fund was an attempt to shake the confidence of the international community in Pakistan.

- A meeting of the Board of Airline Representatives in Pakistan agreed to a 12 percent rise in freight charges which may become effective from mid-December. The Board comprises all domestic and foreign airlines operating in Pakistan.

- The federal budget of 500.2 billion rupees for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) announced in June is being cut to 470 billion rupees as the caretaker government has decided to slash current expenditure (excluding defence budget and debt servicing) by 11.8 percent.

- Maula Bux Abbasi, the dismissed president of the National Bank of Pakistan, the largest state-run bank, was booked in a bank fraud case by the Federal Investigation Agency and was taken into custody for interrogation.
- Akbar Khan, a retired admiral and former chairman of the state-run Karachi Port Trust, was detained by authorities under the maintenance of public order ordinance.
- The government borrowed over 62 billion rupees from the banking sector in the July-October period against a target of 20 billion rupees for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The caretaker cabinet has decided to cut the federal secretariat staff, telephone lines, and staff cars which would bring about an annual saving of 285 million rupees.

- The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources has suggested a six-month study costing 25.08 million rupees on viability of importing natural gas. Pakistan has been looking into the possibility of importing gas from Iran, Qatar and Turkmenistan.
- Money supply during the July-October period rose by about 17 billion rupees, or 1.81 percent, compared to 10.3 billion rupees, or 1.33 percent, in the same period last year.
NAWA-I-WAQT

- Asif Ali Zardari, the detained husband of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, has been shifted to Karachi from Islamabad for investigations into the murder of Murtaza Bhutto, brother of Benazir Bhutto.
- Chief Accountability Commissioner Ghulam Mujaddid Mirza said his office would start investigating corruption cases against senior officials and politicians from Tuesday.
- The first Pakistani trade caravan to Central Asian Republics returned on Monday and brought cement on its return journey.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
